name: DARK SOULS™ II: Scholar of the First Sin

Optimal.Notes: The 40 Hz refresh rate with a matching frame cap delivers smooth, responsive gameplay that suits the deliberate combat pace of Dark Souls II. Medium settings at 1152x720 with FSR upscaling to 1280x800 gives a clean image without taxing the GPU.

profiles.Summary: Dark Souls II: Scholar of the First Sin runs well on the Steam Deck as a Verified title, with its modest 2015 PC requirements sitting comfortably within the Deck's capabilities. The game's DirectX 11 engine translates cleanly through Proton, and the platinum ProtonDB rating with strong confidence suggests a largely trouble-free experience at stable frame rates.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck tuning reports were available; profiles are estimated from the 2015 PC requirements (the Deck's GPU well exceeds the recommended GTX 750/HD 7850), the platinum ProtonDB tier, and the Deck's known hardware capabilities. On first run, check the frame rate in Majula or a large outdoor area and adjust the TDP or resolution if you see sustained dips below your target.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling keeps GPU load very low; the 30 fps lock paired with a 40 Hz refresh gives smooth frame pacing. A 6 W TDP is sufficient for this game at these settings and greatly extends battery life.

KnownIssues: Online multiplayer (invasions/co-op) may require additional network configuration or may be unreliable through Proton
The game uses Games for Windows Live-era DRM remnants and may occasionally show connectivity warnings that can be dismissed
Mouse cursor may appear on screen occasionally; using full controller input avoids this
Some users report needing to set the game to run in a specific Proton version if the default causes launch issues

MaxPerformance.Notes: The Deck's RDNA 2 GPU comfortably exceeds the game's recommended specs, so full 1280x800 at high settings is achievable; expect occasional dips toward 50 fps in dense outdoor areas or heavy particle effects. Disable Motion Blur regardless of setting level as it adds input lag in a precision-combat game.

Optimal.Notes: A solid balance of visual quality and battery life; rendering at 1152x720 with FSR sharpening to native 1280x800 keeps the image clean while staying comfortably within the Deck's power budget. Motion Blur is disabled as it adds little at 60 fps and wastes GPU cycles.

profiles.Summary: Dark Souls II: Scholar of the First Sin runs well on the Steam Deck OLED, benefiting from its Verified status and strong ProtonDB platinum reports. The game's modest PC requirements sit comfortably within the Deck's capabilities, making stable 60 fps achievable at medium-to-high settings without heavy power draw.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the game's 2015 PC requirements (GTX 750 recommended) versus the Deck's roughly GTX 1050 Ti-class GPU, combined with its Verified status and strong ProtonDB platinum trend. On first run, check frame rates in Majula and dense enemy areas — if drops appear at Max Performance, switch to Optimal settings.

MaxBattery.Notes: Aggressive power savings with a locked 30 fps and FSR upscaling from 960x600; the game is very playable at 30 fps given its deliberate combat pacing. GPU clock is manually limited to reduce power draw further.

KnownIssues: Online multiplayer (invasions/co-op) may require additional network configuration and is not guaranteed to work reliably under Proton.
The game uses DirectX 11 via Proton translation, which can occasionally introduce minor stutters during shader compilation on first play.
Mouse cursor may appear on screen in some menus; full controller support resolves most UI issues.
Anti-cheat or Easy Anti-Cheat concerns may affect online play; offline mode is fully functional.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Full native resolution with maximum settings; the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU handles DS2's 2015-era engine comfortably at 15 W, though dense outdoor areas and heavy particle effects may occasionally dip to the low 50s. Shader pre-compilation stutter on first run should subside after the initial session.
